**Triage — graded.** `documentation` · `priority:p3` · `pm:queue` · `domain:devx`; `finding` removed. ⭐ objectstack `finding` box → **0**.

## Verified — and the file contradicts itself

- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx:655` — `| unique | boolean | false | Enforce uniqueness |`
- ⭐ **The same file, `:50`** — `{ name: 'email', …, unique: 'organization' }`. The prop table types it `boolean` while the worked example one page up passes a **string**.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:543-561` documents three spellings: `true` (composite with the org key on an org-scoped object), `'organization'` (the explicit form of the same), `'global'` (installation-wide). ⇒ Not a boolean, and `boolean` is not a narrowing of it — it is a different vocabulary.

⭐ A reader who trusts the table cannot express `'global'` at all, and a reader who copies the example is contradicted by the table on the same page. That self-contradiction is what makes this worth a card rather than a typo fix: either half alone might be read as shorthand; together they leave no correct reading.

## `p3`

Documentation only, and the spec is right. ⛔ Nothing is broken and nothing mis-parses — an author who writes `unique: 'global'` gets what they asked for. The cost is that the table hides two of the three spellings.

## Scope — terminal

Correct the `:655` row to the real vocabulary (`true` / `'organization'` / `'global'`), and ⚠️ **re-derive the autonumber default at `:485-493` against #13894** rather than trusting either the card or this comment — I verified the scope-vocabulary half decisively and ⛔ did **not** verify the autonumber default, so treat that half as *reported, not confirmed*.

⛔ Do not change `field.zod.ts`. The spec is the correct side of this disagreement; the docs move to it.
⚠️ If the prop table is generated rather than hand-written, ⛔ do not hand-edit the output — fix the generator input and regenerate, and say which it was in the report.

## ACCEPT — PR #14941. ⭐ And the PM's assumption 4 was wrong; the dev is right. Recording that plainly.

`domain:devx` seat, session `session_012zGPuVVX3deAx9LdjK8jCk`, R1, 2026-09-03T11:27Z.

### The correction, owned

My dispatch carried assumption 4: that after #13894 an omitted `unique` resolves to `'organization'` on `autonumber`. I flagged it as the half to falsify before writing — and it **is** false. The dev did not take my word for it, and did not take the card's either. Verified independently by me just now:

- **#13894 is OPEN**, assigned to `os-sam`, still `pm:dispatched` in `domain:spec`. It has not landed.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:939` reads `unique: UniqueScopeSchema.default(false)` — **unconditional**, no type branch anywhere near it.

The dev went further than a source read and *measured behaviour*: built `packages/spec` and ran `FieldSchema.safeParse`, getting `autonumber (unique omitted) -> unique=false` and `text (unique omitted) -> unique=false` — **identical**. Then corroborated three independent ways (the unconditional default; the only value-materialising `.overwrite()` handling `deleteBehavior` and early-returning before `unique`, with `superRefine` unable to rewrite values; and the generated reference page stating `false` with no condition).

⇒ Writing the conditional default would have documented a default the schema does not implement — **the exact declared ≠ enforced defect this lane exists to remove**, introduced by the card that was fixing one. Refusing to write it is the single most valuable thing in this delivery.

### The generalizable lesson — worth more than this card

The card's premise was filed by the dev **implementing #13894, from inside its unmerged branch**. From that seat the type-conditional default is real; from the tree's seat it does not exist. ⇒ **A finding filed during implementation of another card describes a future tree, and its "after #X" clauses are unlanded until #X merges.** The card was not wrong to be filed — it was right to be filed — but every "after #X" premise on it needs #X's state re-read at dispatch, not at filing. I under-tested this one: I verified premises 1–3 against `origin/main` and passed premise 4 through as an assumption instead of spending the same 30 seconds on `#13894`'s state.

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | draft, base `main`, first line **`Part of #14901`** — ⭐ not a closing keyword, deliberately, so the card survives to carry the default half |
| governed surface | clean — `content/docs/**` only |
| scope | **+1/−1, one file, one table row** |
| changeset | `skip-changeset` correct — `content/docs/**` is consumed by `apps/docs` (`private: true`); nothing publishes |
| the diff | type cell → `` boolean \| 'global' \| 'organization' ``; default cell **unchanged at `false`**; description carries ADR-0120 scope semantics and the `'tenant'`/`'org'` rejection, matching `field.zod.ts`'s own `.describe()` |

**The convention call was the dev's and it is better than my suggestion.** I proposed a description pointing at the generated reference; the dev matched the spelling of the sibling `multiple` row **directly below it on the same table**, which already ends with a pointer to its own doc block in `FieldSchema`. So the new row is indistinguishable in shape from its neighbour instead of being a one-off in my phrasing. That is the table's convention winning over the dispatcher's wording, which is what I asked for.

### Gates

34 families derived by the dev from the real change set on its own worktree — **not** from any list of mine — with every exit code captured before a pipe. 33 exit 0; 1 declared **NOT MEASURED** (`check-test-completeness` exit 3, argument-less, reads a saved test log — not a red and not a pass). ⭐ Three gates first returned **refusals to measure** (exit 3 / exit 1 on unbuilt `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, and a declaration-less `client-react` dist); the dev built those packages and re-ran all three to a real exit 0 rather than counting a refusal as green. `check-doc-anchors` is the one that covers the new `/docs/references/data/field` link: 295 fragments across 409 files all resolve.

### Follow-up correctly split rather than swept in

**#14940** — the autonumber callout on this same page (`:485`, `:493`) promises *"guarantees a unique, ever-increasing business identifier"*, which the probe shows a bare `autonumber` does **not** get. Filed unassigned and bare for triage, with `Blocked-by: #13894` and a back-link, deduped against the 96 open `documentation` issues first. Not swept in, on the correct ground: the right wording is a **consequence of how #13894 is decided**, not a mechanical substitution — so it is exactly the kind of thing a bounded in-place exemption must refuse.

### Disposition

⇒ **ACCEPT.** CI on `4b8f5f3911` was still converging at 11:27Z (17 success / 10 skipped / 6 in progress) — flip + arm on full green, every check, not the required subset.
**⛔ #14901 does NOT close with this PR.** On merge it goes `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #13894`, carrying the default half. #14940 resolves at the same moment #13894 lands.

### ⭐ The control that matters most here is the cell that did NOT change

The default cell still reads **`false`**, verified explicitly. That is not an omission — it is the deliverable. The card asked for a type-conditional default (`'organization'` on `autonumber`) *"after #13894"*, and #13894 **has not landed**: still `state=open`, assigned `os-sam` in `domain:spec`, re-checked just now. `field.zod.ts` still declares `UniqueScopeSchema.default(false)`, unconditional, and the dev's `safeParse` probe measured `autonumber` and `text` both resolving to `unique=false`.

Writing that conditional default would have documented a default the schema does not implement — the declared ≠ enforced defect this lane exists to remove, introduced by the card fixing one. ⇒ **A probe that confirms a value did not change is a real probe**, and this one is the acceptance criterion for the half that was correctly refused.

### State transition — blocked, not done

`Part of #14901`, so GitHub did not close this card, and it must not be closed: the default half is still owed.

- `pm:dispatched` → **`pm:blocked`**, assignee cleared.
- **Blocked-by: #13894**

When #13894 lands, this card's remaining work is one cell — default → `false` (`'organization'` on `autonumber`) — and **#14940** (the autonumber callout on this same page promising a uniqueness guarantee a bare autonumber does not get) resolves at the same moment. ⇒ The two should be taken together, on a tree where #13894 is actually merged, and the `Blocked-by:` unlock scan should re-verify the file surface at that point rather than trusting this note.
